title: I am, you are
can_do: You can say who and how people are.

grammar.heading: `honaa`: "to be", the whole set
grammar.body: Urdu's "to be" is `honaa`. You've met most of its present forms already; here is the full set. There are only four words, `huuN`, `hai`, `ho` and `haiN`, and each one always goes at the end of the sentence.

grammar.heading: Saying who someone is
grammar.body: Put the person first, then who or what they are, then the verb: `maiN student huuN` is "I student am". Urdu has no word for "a", so that's simply "I'm a student". English job words like `doctor` and `student` are used as they are.

grammar.heading: Respect makes it plural
grammar.body: When you talk about one person you respect, use `haiN`, just as `aap` takes `haiN`. So `imraan saahab doctor haiN` ("Mr Imran is a doctor") is respectful, while `imraan doctor hai` is how you'd talk about a friend. Lesson 4 uses this with your family.

examples.en: Imran is a doctor. (as you'd say it about a friend)

exercises.explanation: `maiN` always takes `huuN`. There's no word for "a".
One person you're talking about takes `hai`. Sana is your partner's younger sister, so no respect plural is needed.
`saahab` shows respect, so the verb is the respectful plural `haiN`, even for one man.
`ham` needs `haiN`. `hai` is for one person or thing.
`aaj` (today) goes at the start or just after `maiN`; the verb `huuN` stays last.
`ham` takes `haiN`. `student` doesn't change: English words don't take an -s in Urdu.

exercises.instruction: Talk about all the children: make it plural.
exercises.explanation: `bacchaa` becomes `bacche` in the plural, and several people take `haiN`.

exercises.hint: Which verb goes with the familiar "you"?

exercises.prompt: Your new neighbour says this as she introduces herself. What is she telling you?

sentence.roman: maiN aaishaa huuN. imraan bhii doctor haiN.
sentence.ur: میں عائشہ ہوں۔ عمران بھی ڈاکٹر ہیں۔
sentence.en: I'm Aisha. Imran is a doctor too.

options: She's Aisha, and Imran is a doctor as well
She's Aisha, and Imran is a student
She's a friend of Imran's, and she's fine
exercises.explanation: `bhii` is "too", so she's a doctor and so is Imran. She says `haiN` about him for respect: he's her husband.

answers.ur: اب میں ٹھیک ہوں، الحمد للہ۔
میں اب ٹھیک ہوں، الحمد للہ۔
الحمد للہ، اب میں ٹھیک ہوں۔
الحمد للہ، میں اب ٹھیک ہوں۔

exercises.explanation: `ab` (now) goes at the start or after `maiN`, and `alhamdulillaah` before or after the rest. You can drop `maiN`, since `huuN` already says "I am".

dialogue.setting: You've just moved into a new house in the UK. Your neighbour Aisha knocks with a plate of food to say hello. Imran is her husband, so she uses the respectful `haiN` about him.
